title: Check your database session
summary: A database client sends SQL to the MariaDB server.
introduction: A database client sends SQL to the MariaDB server. Your task: Read the server name and selected database in the result.
learningObjectives: Read the server name and selected database in the result.
Explain the example for check your database session

blocks.text: A database client sends SQL to the MariaDB server. A session can report the server version and currently selected database.

Use MariaDB 10.11+ with its mariadb client in an empty practice database. These dialect-specific examples do not run in the site's SQLite playground. Keep the sample database separate from real records.

blocks.code: SELECT VERSION() AS server_version,DATABASE() AS current_database;
blocks.title: Check your database session

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The result identifies your MariaDB version and selected database. The database value is NULL if none is selected.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: MariaDB and MySQL are related but not identical. Check the tool and version before copying a version-specific feature.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Read the server name and selected database in the result.
